events.label: Ralph rides alone toward the mountains
events.summary: Free, Ralph rides east through wood and hills toward the mountain wall.

refs.q: though the sight was terrible, yet it gladdened him, since he knew that he was on the right way

opportunities.idea: Biome sequence west of the mountains: forest, open hill-and-dale, coarse uplands, a great pine belt, then the mountain wall.

basis_refs.q: there was a great pine-wood before him

ledger.summary: Ralph rides east alone through the wood by the sun, glad to be free. He follows a woodland stream from the mountains until it turns too far north and sleeps by a pool in a wood-lawn. Next day the thick wood ends in hills and dales with harts and wild swine; he drives a bear from a honey tree and eats the comb, and eats grapes from wild vines on a south-facing slope. He finds the stream again, now running from the east, and sleeps by it; next day he follows it until it turns north, then goes east over hilly land of coarse grass, whin and thorn, seeing the black mountain wall, always climbing, until a great pine wood with no visible end north or south blocks the way late in the afternoon. He rides into it.
ledger.geography_notes: The wood beyond the highway thins; a woodland stream flows from the mountains, its upper course from the east and its lower course turning north. After the thick wood: hills and dales, open, with deer, wild swine, a bear and wild vines on south slopes. Further east: patchy thickets, hilly land with long coarse grass, whin and thorns, rising steadily; then a great pine forest stretching north and south out of sight. The mountain wall is visible like a great black cloud.
